title: Coefficient isomorphism for the first residue
statement:
theorem internal_first_residue_ring_iso
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (E : Type u) [Field E]
    [Algebra (Padic l) E] [FiniteDimensional (Padic l) E] :
    Nonempty (Mon.mk (DerivedNakayama.quotientRing l E 1) ≅
      Mon.mk (IntegralModelsStacks.discreteObj
        (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing l E 1)))

proof.text: Use finite_coefficientExtensionRing at level one. In the absolute-value normed-field presentation defining DerivedNakayama.quotientRing, use the already proved private quotientDiscrete lemma from DerivedNakayamaResolution: it transports the spectral coset neighbourhood basis along equality of the coefficient topologies and proves the actual quotient topology discrete.

On the profinite point construct the ring-presheaf map sending a lifted scalar to its constant continuous function. It is locally surjective: index the finite closed fibres by Fin(card A), whose subtype inclusions are jointly surjective and hence form a coherent cover. Each restricted function is the constant function of its fibre value. It is locally injective: evaluate equality of constant functions at a point; if the constants differ the test object is empty, and use its empty coherent cover.

Mathlib GrothendieckTopology.W_of_isLocallyBijective and W_iff show that sheafification inverts this ring-presheaf map. Compose the resulting isomorphism with the sheafification counit and constantCommuteCompose for CommRingCat to RingCat. This identifies discreteSheaf A with the continuousCoefficientRingSheaf A. Map the isomorphism through sheafCompose for RingCat to Ab, which preserves the canonical ring structures, then apply Mon.mkIso' and invert. At A = coefficientExtensionRing l E 1 its endpoints are definitionally the two ring objects in the unchanged item statement.

The unchanged F3 proof above remains the proof of the public isomorphism theorem. Additional proved private helpers construct the inverse of the actual constant-function map, establish its quotient naturality, and reconcile the integral topologies using coefficientTopology. These helpers supply the normalization needed by InternalFirstResidueRingPushout; they do not replace the landed public proof.

proof_origin.place: first quotient identification; direct ring-sheafification proof on the profinite point, reusing the quotient topology comparison in DerivedNakayamaResolution

normalization_helpers.place: private canonical constant-function inverse and quotient normalization; F3 public proof preserved
